sents.t: In Oakville, summer is very hot.
Today the weather app on my phone says 95 degrees!
At first, I don’t understand.
Ninety-five degrees?
In my country, we use Celsius.
Emma laughs.
“Here we use Fahrenheit. Ninety-five is about thirty-five degrees Celsius.”
The sun is strong, and the sky is blue.
I wear shorts, a T-shirt, and sunglasses, and I drink a lot of water.
Rosa says, “Max doesn’t like hot weather. We walk early in the morning, when it is cool.”
In the afternoon, the sky gets dark.
The wind is strong.
Then, BOOM!
Thunder!
Big rain falls on the streets.
I can’t walk home, so I wait in the bookstore with Emma and a cup of tea.
“Summer storms here are short,” Emma says.
And she is right.
After thirty minutes, the rain stops, and the sun comes out again.
I can see a rainbow over Main Street!
At home, I call my mom.
“How is the weather in America?” she asks.
“Hot, rainy, and sunny, all in one day!” I say.
